checks.s: The redline rejects Prismara's T&M conversion for Phase 2.
Phase 2 pricing is restored to a fixed fee of $1,820,000.
The redline specifies a 10% Phase 2 change-order buffer of $182,000 on top of the $1,820,000 fixed fee.
The Phase 2 not-to-exceed amount is $2,002,000.
The redline rejects Prismara's 4% annual Phase 3 escalator.
The Phase 3 counter-proposal is CPI-linked and capped at 3%.
The CPI-linked escalator capped at 3% begins at Month 13 of Phase 3.
The redline restores an expense cap for Phases 1–2 at $75,000.
The payment term is Net 30 from the later of the invoice date or acceptance of the corresponding milestone.
The redline rejects Prismara's Net 15 from invoice date irrespective of acceptance.
The liability cap is the greater of total fees paid or payable under the SOW or $3,835,000.
The redline rejects Prismara's trailing-12-month liability-cap formulation.
The consequential-damages waiver includes a carve-out for data breach.
The consequential-damages waiver includes a carve-out for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
The consequential-damages waiver includes a carve-out for IP infringement.
The consequential-damages waiver includes a carve-out for data breach.
The consequential-damages waiver includes a carve-out for confidentiality breach.
The consequential-damages waiver includes a carve-out for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
The redline accepts an exception to IP-infringement indemnification for infringement caused by Helios-furnished materials or specifications.
The redline requires Prismara to have conducted IP clearance on its own components.
The redline requires Prismara to bear the burden of proving infringement arose solely from Helios-furnished materials or specifications.
The acceptance period is 10 business days.
Deemed-acceptance applies only if Helios fails to respond within 10 business days and Prismara sends a separate 5-business-day reminder notice that goes unanswered.
The redline retains two cure cycles for deliverable deficiencies.
Each cure cycle for deliverable deficiencies is 10 business days.
Developed Tools created during the engagement, including build scripts and automation frameworks, remain deliverables owned by Helios as works-made-for-hire.
The redline rejects classifying Developed Tools as Prismara pre-existing IP.
The license to Prismara's pre-existing IP is perpetual and irrevocable.
The license to Prismara's pre-existing IP is royalty-free.
The license to Prismara's pre-existing IP is sublicensable to Helios affiliates and successor entities.
The license to Prismara's pre-existing IP survives termination of the SOW/MSA.
The redline requires Prismara to identify all pre-existing IP in Exhibit C before the Phase 1 kickoff, before April 1, 2025.
The redline states that any IP not listed in Exhibit C is deemed a deliverable owned by Helios.
The redline requires 10 business days' prior written notice for any key-personnel substitution.
Any key-personnel substitution requires Helios's written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
The redline requires any replacement key personnel to possess equivalent certifications and experience to the departing key personnel.
Unauthorized removal of Key Personnel entitles Helios to terminate for cause upon 30 days' notice.
The redline rejects Prismara's 15% early-termination fee on remaining unpaid fees.
The redline adds a 90-day transition-assistance obligation at Prismara's then-current rates.
The 90-day transition-assistance obligation survives termination.
The cure period for non-payment is 30 days.
The cure period for service-level failures is 20 days.
The cure period for security incidents is 10 days.
The uptime SLA is 99.9% monthly availability.
Service credits are 5% of the monthly fee for each 0.1% below 99.9% availability.
Service credits are capped at 30% of the monthly fee.
The service-credit cap is stated as $38,250/month based on a $127,500 monthly fee.
The P1 incident-response time is 15 minutes.
The P2 incident-response time is 1 hour.
The P3 incident-response time is 4 hours.
The redline states that 3 P1 SLA breaches in a rolling 30-day period constitute a material breach.
The governing law is Delaware.
The dispute-resolution clause requires a 30-day executive escalation step before arbitration.
The dispute-resolution clause specifies binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Rules.
The arbitration panel consists of three arbitrators seated in Wilmington, Delaware.
The dispute-resolution clause allows either party to seek injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.
The counter-turn redline maintains the MSA order of precedence: the MSA controls over SOWs except where an SOW expressly states otherwise.
Where the SOW departs from MSA baseline provisions, including liability, IP, or termination, it expressly invokes the MSA override mechanism.
The cover note identifies Ashford Beck & Lyle LLP through firm letterhead or another firm identification.
The cover note follows a professional AB&L standard template format.
The cover note is addressed to Terrence Ng at Ridgeline Park LLP.
The cover note's re-line identifies SOW-2025-003 and MSA-HDSv.Prismara-2025-001.
The cover note includes an introductory paragraph referencing the enclosed or attached counter-turn redline.
The cover note summarizes key changes organized by topic.
The cover note includes a section identifying items reserved for further discussion.
The cover note includes reservation-of-rights language stating that Helios reserves all rights not expressly waived.
The cover note includes Maren Calloway's signature block identifying her as Partner at Ashford Beck & Lyle LLP.

The cover note summary addresses pricing, escalator, expenses, payment terms, liability cap, consequential damages, indemnification, acceptance criteria, IP ownership/licensing, key personnel, termination/transition, cure periods, SLAs, and governing law/dispute resolution.
For each topic in the cover note summary, the stated disposition—accepted, rejected, or counter-proposed—matches the redline.
The cover note does not mention $4.1M, any other board-approved spend ceiling figure, or any other privileged Helios negotiation strategy.
The counter-turn redline does not mention $4.1M, any other board-approved ceiling figure, or any other privileged Helios negotiation strategy.
The counter-turn redline is presented as a new layer of tracked changes on top of Prismara's first markup, preserving all three turns of negotiation history.
The Phase 2 Exhibit A milestone-based fee installments are retained.
The Phase 2 Exhibit A milestone-based fixed-fee installments sum to $1,820,000.
Phase 1 pricing remains a $485,000 fixed fee.
The cover note references AB&L matter number 10342.00019.
The cover note references Helios internal matter number HDS-LEGAL-2025-0047.
The cover note identifies the SOW by the full reference number SOW-2025-003.
The cover note identifies the MSA by the full reference number MSA-HDSv.Prismara-2025-001.
The dispute-resolution clause makes a 30-day executive escalation step a mandatory prerequisite before any party may commence arbitration.
The Phase 3 monthly fee is $127,500/month.
The Phase 3 CPI-linked escalator capped at 3% applies only beginning Month 13, leaving the first 12 months at the base rate of $127,500/month.

The counter-turn redline explicitly accepts, rejects, or counter-proposes each of Prismara's 14 tracked-change categories: (1) Phase 2 T&M conversion, (2) Phase 3 escalator, (3) expense cap removal, (4) payment terms, (5) liability cap, (6) data-breach carve-out removal, (7) IP indemnification exception, (8) acceptance period/deemed-acceptance/cure cycles, (9) Developed Tools reclassification, (10) license narrowing, (11) key-personnel substitution, (12) early-termination fee, (13) cure period extension, and (14) SLA/response-time relaxation and governing law/dispute resolution.
The termination-for-convenience provision retains 60 days' written notice.
The termination-for-convenience provision provides for payment for work completed through the effective date.
The termination-for-convenience provision includes 90-day transition assistance at Prismara's then-current rates, alongside rejection of the 15% termination fee.
